education.degree: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science

bullets: Migrated an esports league platform from Google Sites to Next.js with a Supabase backend, replacing manual content updates with live scoring and automated season management.

Cut page load time by 75\% (from 3.2s to 0.8s) by implementing edge caching on Cloudflare, route-based code splitting, and asset optimization for the Next.js frontend.

Doubled the platform's supported environmental data categories (from 2 to 4) by independently implementing end-to-end water and waste data integration, developing Rails backend ingestion pipelines, PostgreSQL schemas, and client-facing React/Vite/Tailwind dashboards.
Engineered asynchronous data pipelines with RabbitMQ, Redis, and Sidekiq to process long-running ingestion jobs in the background, decoupling external API calls from user-facing requests.
Implemented a key client-requested feature by redesigning project-device mapping workflows, refactoring legacy forms to streamline the onboarding of environmental monitoring devices.
Automated software deployment for 100+ devices using Microsoft Deployment Toolkit and created custom USB deployment solution for Windows 11, reducing deployment time by 40\%
Managed 200+ user accounts and permissions via NAS, conducting access audits and boosting system uptime by 15\%

projects.name: Hermes Letters
projects.technologies: Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, Drizzle ORM, PostgreSQL
bullets: Built a private long-form messaging platform for a group of 20+ friends during a study abroad semester, delivering 30+ letters.
Ensured consistent letter claims via atomic SQL updates and secured sessions in XSS-resistant httpOnly cookies.
Derived user connections at query time from kept-letter records using indexed lookups, avoiding a separate relationship table and associated database sync issues.
Hardened media storage by validating uploads via server-side magic-byte signatures, storing files in a private Supabase bucket, and restricting delivery to 1-hour signed URLs.

projects.name: Persephone
projects.technologies: Python, Cython, Rust, FastAPI, React/TypeScript, Kalshi, Low-Latency
bullets: Built and launched a production Kalshi prediction-market trading system that generated $\sim$\$8K net PnL over its first 4 days of live trading and traded $\sim$\$200K in volume across model-driven quoting, exchange execution, risk controls, and operator tooling.

Cut live hot-path latency by rewriting 9 performance-critical Python kernels into native Cython extensions for orderbook processing, OBI evaluation, RTI/event aggregation, threshold storage, and theo prediction.
Built fail-closed market-data infrastructure that blocks stale, crossed, overflowed, or low-venue feeds before they reach the quoting path, using trusted-spot checks and venue-health state machines.

Built a write-ahead order safety layer that records order intent before exchange dispatch, reducing duplicate-send and crash-replay risk with deterministic client IDs, final risk gates, and durable execution records.
Prevented unsafe model and release promotion with walk-forward validation, Brier/reliability gates, SHA-256 model manifests, immutable release artifacts, latency SLOs, and shadow-readiness checks.

Implemented a 14-crate Rust replacement core for deterministic low-latency execution, using fixed-point arithmetic, typed event protocols, replay-golden tests, allocation audits, and canonical state digests.

projects.name: Self-Hosted Media \& Application Server
